text:
kevin: quick idea — run a small experiment to route free/starter tiers to a low-cost variant in EU/APAC off-peak. goal: ~50–70% token $ reduction w/ <2% quality regression and p95 < 400ms. safe to start a canary?

maria (product): important to surface this in billing/console. customers must know when cheaper variant used. also need opt-out for paid tiers.

oliver (eng-platform): technically doable. we have policy engine that can route by tier+region+time. suggest a canary: 10% traffic on starter in eu-west during 01:00-06:00 UTC.

kevin: thinking variant = "redwood-small-8q" (quantized) vs baseline "redwood-base-16f". routing rule rough sketch: 
```json
{
  "match": {"tier": ["free","starter"], "region": ["eu-west","ap-southeast"]},
  "time_window": "01:00-06:00",
  "variant_priority": ["redwood-small-8q","redwood-base-16f"],
  "percent": 10
}
```

suresh (eng-runtime): watch out for kv-cache warmup and context length differences. quantized path drops perf on long-seq generation. we should gate by expected seq < 1024 and add prefix cache warmers. also metric for repeat token churn.

lisa (telemetry): add events: `routing.variant_assigned`, `routing.fallback_trigger`, `routing.cost_delta`. emit sample tags: tier, region, prompt_len, p50_latency, p95_latency, token_count, variant. dashboard panels: cost-per-1k-tokens by tier, quality-regression (bleu/accept-rate) by test prompt set.

sam (console): UX props — show a subtle nudge on the project settings and per-route: "We may use a frugal model variant for Starter during off-peak hours to lower costs. Click to preview expected quality and opt out." Add toggle + expand to show example outputs side-by-side. Proposed quick copy: 
"Redwood may serve a budget variant for your Starter plan during off-peak hours to reduce token costs by ~60%. Opt-out or pin a model in Settings."

anya (oncall): set alerts: error-rate delta > 1% OR fallback rate > 5% triggers page. autopolicy: if fallback reason == "quality_regress" then auto-switch users back to baseline variant for 30m, and escalate.

oliver (eng-platform): rollout command suggestion: `redwoodctl routes apply --name frugal-tier-eu --spec frugal-policy.json --pct 10 --start 2026-05-10T01:00Z --end 2026-05-10T06:00Z`. deploy-bot: starting canary when you say the word.

deploy-bot: canary rollout queued: frugal-tier-eu @ 10%.

kevin: also want budget guards at per-customer level — customer token budget per month, and soft-degrade to frugal variant when spend > X% of budget. Idea: meter & mark in header `X-Rdwd-Routed-Variant` and `X-Rdwd-Cost-Delta` for billing.

lisa (telemetry): emit per-customer cost_estimate event so billing can surface projected spend. also we can compute unit_cost = measured_cost / tokens and visualize bimonthly.

suresh: add a small A/B eval harness — 2k prompts sampled from live requests (anonymized) run through both variants and compute acceptance rate + perplexity delta. run daily and alert if regression > 3%.

maria (product): schedule review in next product sync. we need privacy sign-off for sampling pipeline and clear console language.

sam (console): follow-ups — expose a small histogram in route detail: %requests routed to frugal variant, avg cost delta, and quality score trend. also toggle for per-customer opt-out.

kevin: action items: oliver to draft policy + rollout command, suresh to define warmup and seq gating, lisa to add telemetry events and dashboards, sam to mock nudge copy/UI, anya to propose SLO/alerts, maria to coordinate product sign-off. aiming to start 10% canary next week.

anya (oncall): please add runbook snippet for rollback: `redwoodctl routes update --name frugal-tier-eu --pct 0` and page if fallback_rate > 5% for 15m.

kevin: thanks all — if we can keep regressions minimal this should be a big win for starter economics. :thumbsup: 

oliver (eng-platform): I'll push a draft policy to the repo today and ping the channel with link.

sam (console): will mock the nudge screenshots by EOD.

maria (product): adding to agenda.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: frugal-tier-eu @ 10% (initiated by oliver)
